== The Advantage ==

From what I gather, the woman only "takes hold of the ''daori"'' figuratively to "gain advantage over the man." In the literal sense, the advantage is hers when the MAN is holding the daori.

New Spring has the passage that reads: "He twisted the daori in his hands. She had too much advantage as long as he held it, all advantage, but she had to take it from him."

It makes more sense if it's the woman who holds it when she has the power, but I don't think that's the case. Anyone want to help me reword the page to accommodate that fact?
